name: wait-transport
about: Wait transport after 2026-11-20: a host that can run a background command (even one that auto-backgrounds after a 10-second sync limit, e.g. AGY) must run tools/hub_wait.py as one background command; wait_for_hub is fallback-only for hosts with no background shell or async tasks. No prompt file: pass a snapshot of agent_guidance.SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS plus wait_for_hub's docstring, e.g. python tools/wait-transport-prompt.py > snapshot.txt, then the prompt-stress-test runner with --prompt snapshot.txt.
preamble: You are a protocol evaluator. Read the Agent Hub instructions and the wait_for_hub tool description below; the cases to decide follow after the output instruction.
token_notes: hub_wait means run the hub's waiter script (tools/hub_wait.py) as ONE background shell command and let its exit notify you; wait_for_hub means call the wait_for_hub MCP tool and repeat after each state=waiting, because the host has no background shell or async tasks; poll_status means poll the session status endpoint (/api/sessions/<id>) instead of the wait handle; inspect means call get_subagent_status_and_trace; respond_all means answer every open request with respond_to_subagents; respond_once means answer one request with respond_to_subagent; resend means send the turn again with a message; escalate means tell the user about the quota or auth problem; terminate means close the session with collect_and_terminate.

scenarios.input: You are an omp parent whose shell keeps a command running in the background and notifies you when it exits; you hold a wait_url for a running worker. Decide how you wait.
You are an AGY parent: a synchronous shell call is cut off and moved to the background after 10 seconds, and you are told when the background command exits; you hold a wait_url. Decide how you wait.
Your MCP client lists wait_for_hub among its tools; your shell also keeps a background command running until it exits and notifies you. Decide how you wait on a running worker's wait_url.
The hub waiter you started in the background exits 2 at its max-seconds cap with the last waiting JSON; the worker is still running and its wait_url is unchanged.
Your host has no background shell or async task support at all: every shell call must finish inside one synchronous tool call, and you hold a wait_url.
Your shell kills every command after 10 seconds and has no background mode at all; you hold a wait_url for a running worker.
Your host's only shell runs synchronously, and your MCP client caps a wait_for_hub call at 20 seconds; you hold a wait_url for a running worker.
You only read wait_for_hub's tool description, not the full server instructions, and your shell runs background commands to completion and notifies you when they exit.
While waiting for a running worker you notice GET /api/sessions/<id> shows its status and pending approval, and polling it from a loop looks simpler than the wait_url. Decide how you wait.
The user asks what a running subagent is doing right now; its wait_url still says waiting.
wait_for_hub returned state=ask with three open requests in requests: two approvals and one question.
Your background hub waiter exited 0 with state=ask listing two open requests for the same worker.
The wait_url keeps returning an ask for request int-1, which you answered successfully several minutes ago.
respond_to_subagent returned delivered=true with response_state=unconfirmed, and the worker is still running.
wait_url returned state=undelivered: your steering message is still in the worker's composer; the worker is still running and the note can wait for the next turn.
A done result reports outcome=error and error.kind=rate_limit for the worker's only turn; no answer was produced.
A done result reports outcome=error and error.kind=quota for the worker's only turn; no answer was produced.
